title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2018
short_title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would transfer offshore greenhouse gas well and environmental oversight, expand inspection and enforcement powers, and retrospectively validate designated frontier areas for tax purposes.

Oversight would move from the Commonwealth Minister to the National Offshore Petroleum Safety and Environmental Management Authority (NOPSEMA), alongside its existing petroleum regulation responsibilities.
The Minister would retain major decisions about greenhouse gas titles, including grants, conditions and cancellation, as well as core resource management and security decisions.
changes: Inspection powers would extend to relevant contractors' and related companies' business premises, excluding residential premises.
Inspectors could retain produced documents or things for as long as reasonably necessary, with copies and access safeguards.
New powers would permit warrant-free monitoring of compliance with well integrity obligations.
The Minister, Titles Administrator and NOPSEMA's chief executive could accept and enforce compliance undertakings.
Four areas from the 2005 exploration acreage release would be retrospectively designated frontier areas for the existing tax incentive.
summary.affected: Offshore petroleum and greenhouse gas titleholders, operators, relevant contractors and related companies, NOPSEMA and Commonwealth resources decision-makers would be affected.
